description: A sixteen-step drum sequencer with eight gate tracks, sixteen storable patterns and an eight-slot chain that plays those patterns in order.

params.text: Switches that step of that track on or off; a step that is on sends a gate from its track's jack when the sequence reaches it.
Starts and stops the sequencer; each press flips it, and the lamp is lit while it runs.
Raises the number of the pattern loaded on the pads by one, to a maximum of 16.
Lowers the number of the pattern loaded on the pads by one, to a minimum of 1.
Raises the pattern number in that slot of the chain by one, to a maximum of 16.
Lowers the pattern number in that slot of the chain by one; at 0 the slot is skipped, and the first slot never goes below 1.
Chooses whether the sequencer moves on to the next chain slot at the end of the sixteen steps or keeps repeating the pattern now loaded.
Copies the sixteen by eight grid now on the pads into a holding buffer.
Writes the grid held by COPY onto the pads, replacing the pattern now loaded.

inputs.text: Advances the sequence by one step each time the voltage rises through 0.5V.
Flips the sequencer between running and stopped each time the voltage rises through 0.5V.
Flips chaining on and off each time the voltage rises through 0.5V.
Returns the sequence to the first of its sixteen steps and loads the pattern named by the first chain slot, each time the voltage rises through 0.5V.
Chooses which of the 16 patterns is loaded on the pads, one pattern for every 0.588V from 0V upward; while a cable is patched here the up and down buttons are overridden every sample.
Sets the pattern number in that slot of the chain, one pattern for every 0.588V from 0V upward, with anything below 0.588V leaving the slot empty so it is skipped.

outputs.text: 5V while that track's step is on, for the first 505 samples after each clock rise.

notes: nothing moves until a clock is patched into CLOCK; the sequencer comes up running and chaining, but it has no time base of its own.
the knob that would set the gate length is left out of the panel, so every gate is a fixed 505 samples long whatever the tempo.
the eight row labels name a drum kit, but each row is a plain gate output and the label changes nothing about it.
